faqs.question: How much does restumping cost in Ballarat?
faqs.answer: Restumping in the Ballarat area typically runs about $400–$700 per stump. A smaller weatherboard home with around 50 stumps often lands near $8,000–$9,000, while larger homes with 100+ stumps can exceed $16,000. Levelling floors or replacing damaged joists adds to the total, so comparing a few local quotes is the best way to price your job.

faqs.question: How do I know if my Ballarat home needs restumping?
faqs.answer: Tell-tale signs include sloping or bouncy floors, doors and windows that stick, cracks in plaster or cornices, and gaps opening between walls and skirting. Older homes on original timber stumps are most at risk in the region's cold, damp conditions.

faqs.question: Do I need a building permit to restump a house in Victoria?
faqs.answer: Yes. Restumping (reblocking) is building work in Victoria and requires a building permit through a registered building surveyor. A registered restumping contractor will normally arrange the permit and inspections as part of the job.

faqs.question: Why do Bendigo homes need restumping so often?
faqs.answer: Central Victoria's reactive clay soils swell in winter and shrink in Bendigo's hot, dry summers, and that constant movement lifts and drops house stumps over time. Combined with ageing timber stumps in the region's older homes, it's a common cause of uneven, cracking floors.

faqs.question: Is restumping the same as underpinning?
faqs.answer: Not quite. Restumping (reblocking) replaces the stumps a timber-floored house sits on, while underpinning strengthens the footings beneath a slab or masonry wall. A local contractor can advise which your home actually needs after an inspection.

faqs.question: How much do NDIS home modifications cost in Townsville?

faqs.question: How much does a deceased estate cleanout cost in Bendigo?
faqs.answer: In regional Victoria a deceased estate cleanout typically runs about $800–$5,000 depending on the size of the property and the volume of belongings. Pricing is often based on volume (roughly $75 per cubic metre) or the crew's time ($150–$250 per hour for a lead). Sorting, donations and a pre-sale clean can affect the final figure, so it's worth comparing a couple of local quotes.

faqs.question: What happens to belongings during an estate clearance?
faqs.answer: A good clearance works to the family's instructions: heirlooms and documents are set aside, usable furniture and goods are donated to charity or sold, and only the remainder is removed and disposed of. Nothing of value is thrown out without your say-so.
